newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up slightly despite softer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up slightly despite softer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended up slightly Friday in a moderate session, helped by some technical buying when downside momentum stalled early in the day despite reports of softer physical prices, sources said.
September edged up 0.4 cent to close at $2.432 per million British thermal units. October settled 0.7 cent higher at $2.464. Other deferreds ended up by 0.8 to 3.5 cents.

"We tested sub-$2.40 (basis September) and couldn't blow through it, so we came back, but there wasn't much reason to move up much either," said one East Coast trader, noting cash was down slightly but relatively firm for a weekend.
Traders said foreasts for warmer Midwest and East Coast weekend weather helped limit the weekend cash slide, but cooler temperatures next week could put the physical market on the defensive.
But with cash still well-above the screen, supply/demand relatively tight and concerns lingering about storage, few expected the cash to crater near-term regardless of weather.
"Weather has not been driving this market," another East Coast trader said, noting fund and technical buying helped back the recent rally.

Technical traders still pegged September resistance at yesterday's high of $2.55 and then at the contract high and double top at $2.605. Further selling was likely at the $2.64-2.655 spot continuation chart gap from late January. Support was seen at $2.395, $2.34 and $2.30, with better buying likely in the $2.25-2.27 area.

In the cash Friday, Gulf Coast weekend prices slipped slightly to about the $2.50 level. Midcon pipes were steady to modestly lower in the low-$2.40s. New York city gate gas was little changed in the mid-$2.70s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip gained 1.8 cents to $2.353. NYMEX volume figures were not available today.

On the KCBT, September finished 2.2 cents higher at $2.362, while deferreds ended steady to up three cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.8 cents to 7.0 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 277 lots traded, down from Thursday's total of 368.
